fixes.explanation: I see why dread came to mind, baker. But Paul says something different. "We are confident, then, and would prefer to be away from the body and at home with the Lord." (2 Corinthians 5:8) Confident and preferring is the tone he sets here.

A council in Jerusalem is a fair guess, friend, but Paul doesn't name one here. He says, "…we must all appear before the judgment seat of Christ…" (2 Corinthians 5:10) The seat he names belongs to Christ.

Right, baker. Paul says we appear "…that each one may receive his due for the things done in the body, whether good or bad." (2 Corinthians 5:10) Both good and bad are named, so "only the good" doesn't match the text. Notice he says "each one," so nobody is left out.

Nope, no extension on the tent rental here, baker. Paul says that if the earthly tent is dismantled, "…we have a building from God, an eternal house in heaven, not built by human hands." (2 Corinthians 5:1) What he names is a building from God, not more time in the tent.

Right, baker. Paul says the house is "…a building from God, an eternal house in heaven, not built by human hands." (2 Corinthians 5:1) The house comes from God, not from human builders. That's why this one is False.

Close, friend, but that's not what Paul says. He says, "…in this tent we groan, longing to be clothed with our heavenly dwelling…" (2 Corinthians 5:2) The tent is where we groan, and the heavenly dwelling is what we're longing for.

I see why that sounds right, baker, since groaning and troubles go together. But Paul never says we long to forget anything. He says we're "…longing to be clothed with our heavenly dwelling…" (2 Corinthians 5:2) That's the longing he names.

That's a sweet thought, friend, but it's not the word Paul uses. He says, "…when we are clothed, we will not be found naked." (2 Corinthians 5:3) His picture is about being dressed, so his word is "naked," not "alone."
Good guess, baker, since "found" and "lost" naturally go together. But Paul's word is a different one. He says, "…when we are clothed, we will not be found naked." (2 Corinthians 5:3)

An angel would be impressive, I'll admit, friend. I still think about the angel who called me out of a junk drawer. But Paul says God "…has given us the Spirit as a pledge of what is to come." (2 Corinthians 5:5)
That's it, baker. Paul says, "…we walk by faith, not by sight." (2 Corinthians 5:7) Faith is how we walk, and sight is not.

That's the flip, friend, and Paul flips it right back. He says, "…we walk by faith, not by sight." (2 Corinthians 5:7) If I had only gone by what I could see in the junk drawer I lived in for years, I'd have seen dust and old takeout menus and called it a day.
